audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Elisha miracle cycle: widow, Shunammite, food, and famine narratives, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for debt slavery threat, widow's oil economy, Shunammite hospitality and agency, promised child, child death and restoration, Gehazi's boundary failure, famine stew, and barley feeding.

verses.restored: One woman from wives of sons of prophets cried to Elisha, saying, Your servant my husband died, and you know your servant feared YHWH; the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves.
Elisha said to her, What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house? She said, Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.
He said, Go, ask for vessels from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels; do not make few.
Then go in and shut the door behind you and your children; pour into all these vessels, and set aside the full ones.
She went from him and shut the door behind her and her children; they were bringing vessels to her, and she was pouring.
When vessels were full, she said to her son, Bring me another vessel. He said, There is no more vessel. And oil stopped.
She came and told man of Divine. He said, Go, sell oil and pay your debt; you and your children shall live on what remains.
One day Elisha passed to Shunem. There was a great woman there, and she held him strongly to eat bread. Whenever he passed, he turned aside there to eat bread.
She said to her husband, Look, I know this is a holy man of Divine passing by us continually.
Let us make a small upper room with walls, and put for him there a bed, table, chair, and lamp, so when he comes to us he may turn aside there.
One day he came there, turned aside to upper room, and lay there.
He said to Gehazi his young man, Call this Shunammite. He called her, and she stood before him.

He said to him, Say to her, Look, you have trembled/been careful for us with all this care; what may be done for you? Is there something to speak for you to king or army commander? She said, I dwell among my people.
He said, What then may be done for her? Gehazi said, Truly she has no son, and her husband is old.
He said, Call her. He called her, and she stood at doorway.
He said, At this season, at time of life, you shall embrace a son. She said, No, my lord, man of Divine, do not lie to your servant woman.
The woman conceived and bore a son at that season, at time of life, as Elisha spoke to her.
The child grew. One day he went out to his father, to harvesters.
He said to his father, My head, my head! The father said to the young man, Carry him to his mother.
He carried him and brought him to his mother; he sat on her knees until noon, and died.
She went up, laid him on bed of man of Divine, shut door behind him, and went out.
She called to her husband and said, Please send me one servant and one donkey, that I may run to man of Divine and return.
He said, Why are you going to him today? It is not new moon or Sabbath. She said, Shalom.
She saddled donkey and said to her young man, Drive and go; do not hold back riding for me unless I tell you.
She went and came to man of Divine at Mount Carmel. When man of Divine saw her from opposite, he said to Gehazi, Look, that Shunammite.
Now run to meet her and say, Is shalom with you? Is shalom with your husband? Is shalom with the child? She said, Shalom.

When she came to man of Divine at mountain, she grasped his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but man of Divine said, Let her alone, for her soul is bitter in her, and YHWH has hidden it from me and not told me.
She said, Did I ask a son from my lord? Did I not say, Do not deceive me?
He said to Gehazi, Gird your waist, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not bless him; if anyone blesses you, do not answer. Put my staff on face of the boy.
Mother of the boy said, As YHWH lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. He arose and went after her.
Gehazi passed before them and put staff on face of boy, but there was no voice and no attention. He returned to meet him and told him, The boy has not awakened.
Elisha came into house, and look, the boy was dead, laid on his bed.
He went in, shut door behind the two of them, and prayed to YHWH.
He went up and lay upon the child, placing his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his palms on his palms; he stretched himself upon him, and flesh of child grew warm.
He returned and walked in house once here and once there; he went up and stretched himself upon him, and boy sneezed seven times, and boy opened his eyes.
He called Gehazi and said, Call this Shunammite. He called her. She came to him, and he said, Lift up your son.
She came, fell at his feet, bowed to ground, lifted up her son, and went out.
Elisha returned to Gilgal, and famine was in land. Sons of prophets were sitting before him. He said to his young man, Put on large pot and boil stew for sons of prophets.
One went out to field to gather herbs and found a wild vine; he gathered from it wild gourds, his garment full, came and sliced them into pot of stew, for they did not know.
They poured out for men to eat. When they ate from stew, they cried and said, Death in the pot, man of Divine! They could not eat.
He said, Bring flour. He threw it into pot and said, Pour for people, and let them eat. There was no evil thing in pot.
A man came from Baal-shalishah and brought man of Divine bread of firstfruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh grain in his sack. He said, Give to people, and let them eat.
His servant said, How can I set this before one hundred men? He said, Give to people, and let them eat, for thus says YHWH: Eating, they shall eat, and leaving over, they shall leave over.
He set before them; they ate and left over, according to word of YHWH.

translation_notes: The widow's crisis is economic violence: debt threatens to turn children into slaves. The miracle prevents family separation and debt slavery rather than romanticizing poverty.
The Shunammite woman is called great, initiates hospitality, designs a room, refuses court patronage, and later confronts the prophet directly.
The promised child is not proof that childlessness was shameful or that every generous person is owed a child.
The woman's protest, 'Did I ask a son?' names the cruelty of receiving a promise and then losing the child.
Gehazi tries to push away a grieving mother; Elisha stops him. Grief and bodily urgency deserve access, not gatekeeping.
The child-revival scene is intimate and strange; it must not become a technique or justification for unsafe contact.
The poisoned stew and barley feeding keep prophetic power close to public food safety during famine.
Firstfruits become shared food, not prestige property.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 4 to justify debt slavery, poverty romanticizing, reproductive pressure, miracle manipulation, unsafe healing practices, or gatekeeping grief. Center debt relief, food security, women's agency, honest protest after child loss, and communal nourishment.
